[[EXPERIMENT_TITLE]] - Loading Isotherm Determination Report

Experiment Information

Experiment ID: [[EXPERIMENT_ID]]

Process ID: [[PROCESS_ID]]

Start Date: [[EXPERIMENT_DATE]]

End Date / Report Date: [[REPORT_DATE]]

Objective

Determination of loading isotherms for [[LIGAND_NAME]] binding to the resin at different salt concentrations ([[SALT_CONCENTRATION_UNIT]]) using an automated robotic workflow integrating Opentrons OT-2, UR5 robot arm, vacuum manifold, and Tecan Spark platereader.

Methods

Experimental Conditions
  • Ligand: [[LIGAND_NAME]]
  • Ligand stock concentration: [[LIGAND_STOCK_CONCENTRATION]] [[LIGAND_CONCENTRATION_UNIT]]
  • Ligand concentration range: [[LIGAND_CONCENTRATIONS]] ([[NUMBER_OF_LIGAND_CONCENTRATIONS]] levels)
  • Resin mass per well: [[RESIN_MASS]]
  • Buffer: [[BUFFER]]
  • Salt: [[SALT_NAME]]
  • Salt stock concentration: [[SALT_STOCK_CONCENTRATION]] [[SALT_CONCENTRATION_UNIT]]
  • Salt concentration range: [[SALT_CONCENTRATIONS]] ([[NUMBER_OF_SALT_CONCENTRATIONS]] levels)
  • Total volume per well: [[TOTAL_VOLUME]]
  • Incubation temperature: [[INCUBATION_TEMPERATURE]]
  • Incubation shaker speed: [[SHAKER_SPEED_INCUBATION]]
  • Incubation time: [[INCUBATION_TIME]]
  • Number of technical replicates: [[REPLICATES]]
  • Measurement wavelength: [[MEASUREMENT_WAVELENGTH]] nm
  • Calibration curve slope: [[CALIBRATION_CURVE_SLOPE]]
  • Calibration curve intercept: [[CALIBRATION_CURVE_INTERCEPT]]
Automated Workflow Overview

The loading isotherm experiment was executed using an integrated automated workflow combining an Opentrons OT-2 liquid handling robot, a UR5 robotic arm, a vacuum manifold with controllable pump, and a Tecan Spark platereader. The following steps summarize the process:

  1. Initial plate setup and equilibration preparation
    • The Opentrons OT-2 was initialized with a custom 96-well filter plate labware definition (cytiva_96_filterwellplate_1ml.json) and programmed to dispense equilibration buffer [[BUFFER]] and ligand/salt solutions according to the specified ligand ([[LIGAND_CONCENTRATIONS]]) and salt ([[SALT_CONCENTRATIONS]]) concentration matrix.
    • The UR5 robot grabbed a 96-deep well plate ("96DeepWP") from storage (Storage2) and placed it on the vacuum manifold position (Pump_Pos1) to serve as the collection plate.
    • The UR5 placed the vacuum manifold onto the pump position and transferred the equilibrated filter plate from the OT-2 position (OT2_Pos1) onto the vacuum manifold (Pump_Pos2).
  2. Vacuum-assisted equilibration
    • The VacuuPump applied vacuum at a pump speed of [[PUMP_SPEED]] for [[PUMP_DURATION]] seconds to pull liquid through the filter plate into the deep well plate, followed by a venting step of [[VENTING_TIME]] seconds to release vacuum.
    • The UR5 returned the filter plate from the vacuum position (Pump_Pos2) back to the OT-2 position (OT2_Pos1) for subsequent processing.
  3. Automated equilibration cycles
    • A loop of [[EQUILIBRATION_CYCLES]] equilibration cycles was executed. For each cycle, the OT-2 dispensed equilibration buffer with a volume of [[EQUILIBRATION_VOLUME]] into the filter plate according to the protocol.
    • After dispensing, the UR5 moved the filter plate to the vacuum manifold (Pump_Pos2), the VacuuPump again ran at [[PUMP_SPEED]] for [[EQUILIBRATION_CYCLE_DURATION]] seconds per cycle, followed by venting, and the UR5 returned the plate to the OT-2 position.
  4. Post-equilibration handling and ligand loading
    • After the equilibration loop, the UR5 removed the vacuum manifold and returned the 96-deep well plate to storage.
    • The OT-2 then executed protocols (with the custom filter plate labware) to dispense [[LIGAND_NAME]] solutions at the defined concentration levels ([[LIGAND_CONCENTRATIONS]]) and salt concentrations ([[SALT_CONCENTRATIONS]]) into the equilibrated resin in the filter plate, up to a total volume of [[TOTAL_VOLUME]] per well.
    • User-guided pauses were included (e.g. covering the filter plate with foil, refreshing tips, and clearing waste) to ensure proper handling of consumables and to protect light-sensitive ligands if relevant.
    • After incubation on a shaker at [[INCUBATION_TEMPERATURE]] and [[SHAKER_SPEED_INCUBATION]] for [[INCUBATION_TIME]], the UR5 transferred a fresh 96-deep well plate to the vacuum position, placed the vacuum manifold, and again positioned the filter plate over the deep well plate.
    • The VacuuPump ran at [[PUMP_SPEED]] for [[PUMP_DURATION]] seconds to separate liquid from the resin, followed by venting. The UR5 then stored the filter plate and moved the deep well plate (containing the post-binding supernatants) to the OT-2 deck (OT2_Pos5).
  5. Preparation of measurement plate and transfer to Tecan Spark
    • The UR5 placed a fresh microplate ("WP1") on the OT-2 deck (OT2_Pos1).
    • The OT-2 executed a transfer protocol to distribute supernatant samples from the deep well plate into the measurement plate (WP1) for absorbance/fluorescence measurement at [[MEASUREMENT_WAVELENGTH]] nm.
    • The UR5 then transferred the measurement plate WP1 to the Tecan Spark, where the reader was opened, the plate was loaded, the door closed, and the programmed measurement run was executed.
    • After measurement, the plate was removed from the Tecan Spark by the UR5 and returned to storage (Storage4).

The measured signals were converted to equilibrium ligand concentrations using the calibration curve (slope [[CALIBRATION_CURVE_SLOPE]], intercept [[CALIBRATION_CURVE_INTERCEPT]]), and the amount of ligand bound to the resin was calculated from mass balance using the known initial ligand concentration, equilibrium concentration, total volume [[TOTAL_VOLUME]], and resin mass [[RESIN_MASS]]. Loading isotherms were compiled for each salt concentration level.

Results

Loading Isotherms of [[LIGAND_NAME]] on Resin at Different [[SALT_NAME]] Concentrations
[[PLOT_1]]

Figure 1: Loading isotherms of [[LIGAND_NAME]] on the resin for different [[SALT_NAME]] concentrations ([[SALT_CONCENTRATIONS]]; unit: [[SALT_CONCENTRATION_UNIT]]). Each curve shows the equilibrium bound amount of ligand per mass of resin as a function of the equilibrium ligand concentration in solution. Data are based on [[REPLICATES]] replicates per condition, using calibration at [[MEASUREMENT_WAVELENGTH]] nm.

Additional analysis and interpretation of the loading isotherms (e.g. model fitting, capacity estimation, and comparison across salt conditions) can be documented here by the experimenter.
